DMCFingerTurnEasy.parity_note: parity_interior_min is NOT relaxed: interior-pixel agreement measures exactly 1.000000 -- 0 bad pixels out of 9,834,291 -- over 201 independent draws of 64 states at the shipped default_supersample = 1. What is declared is parity_all_exact_min, and the reason is arithmetic rather than a tolerance -- all-pixel exactness is interior exactness WEIGHTED BY HOW MUCH OF THE FRAME MOVES, and finger-turn_easy's seven movers cover 11.7% of an 84 px frame against cartpole's 2.5%. Measured over those 201 draws: all-pixel 0.9103 at WORST and 0.9119 median, i.e. it CLEARS the shared 0.90 bar on every draw -- the floor is declared so that the margin is the scene's rather than luck's, and it is set from a draw count rather than from one large evaluation, because a rare pixel event reported off a single draw is how MujocoPusher came to declare a floor it then failed 15 times in 101. 100.0% of every disagreeing pixel is inside the ray-cast mover pass and the baked plate is 1.00000 exact on the pixels it owns; the residual is a one-level rim on curved silhouettes, where MuJoCo shades a tessellated capsule per vertex and an analytic per-pixel evaluation lands within a few levels of it. finger-spin (0.9288 worst) and finger-turn_hard (0.9241 worst) are the same renderer with fewer mover pixels and declare nothing. Dropping the supersample IMPROVED all three -- at ss=2 the same draws gave 0.9053 / 0.9249 / 0.9200 -- because an aliased edge is bit-identical to MuJoCo wherever MuJoCo's own MSAA happened to be fully covered, while a blended edge almost never is.

DMCManipulatorBringBall.docstring: DM Control manipulator-bring_ball at camera 0. State is qpos plus whatever the episode draws into the model; the frame is a measured pure function of it.
DMCManipulatorBringBall.state_dims_note: Three of fifteen dimensions -- ball_y, target_ball_quat_qw and target_ball_quat_qy -- are EXCLUDED from check_state_dims_matter as render-invariant, under the validated contract that check documents. They are not dead and they are not undrawn: they are geometrically incapable of changing THIS renderer's image, and the reason is a property of the solid rather than of the implementation. All three orient an UNTEXTURED SPHERE -- `ball` is sphere size=.022 on material `self`, `target_ball` is sphere size=.02 on material `target`, and neither material carries a texture -- and a sphere is a surface of revolution about every axis through its centre, so an analytic per-pixel intersector returns the same hit point, the same normal and therefore the same colour for every rotation of it. Exactly, not approximately. NOTHING IS EXCLUDED BY NAME: this class only OFFERS the three (RENDER_INVARIANT_DIMS), and check_state_dims_matter grants the exclusion only after verifying against the compiled model that perturbing the dimension changes nothing but the geom_xmat of SPHERE geoms -- geom_xpos, geom_size, geom_type, every non-sphere orientation and every material, light and camera array bit-identical. A dimension the renderer merely failed to draw moves one of those and is refused. Each granted exclusion is REPORTED in the check's excluded_dims with its reason; none of them is a silent pass. MEASURED, both directions. Under the default (sphere) appearance the three move 0 pixels here at 224 px and at 84 px, while the OFFICIAL renderer moves 896 px at max 55/255 for ball_y and 734 px at max 33/255 for each quaternion slot -- MuJoCo draws a sphere as a TESSELLATED mesh shaded PER VERTEX, so rotating it moves the Gouraud interpolation and the specular vertex. That residual is the same class this family already declares as a one-level rim on curved silhouettes: it is bounded (all-pixel exactness after each perturbation is 0.98275-0.98277 against a 0.98280 baseline, interior-pixel agreement stays 1.000000), and closing it would mean reproducing MuJoCo's icosphere tessellation in the mover pass for EVERY DM Control cell to recover ~800 px at <= 55/255 on one of them. AND THE EXCLUSION EVAPORATES WHEN THE GEOMETRY CHANGES, which is what makes it a statement about spheres rather than about rotation: under target_ball.shape = 0 the target is a BOX, the validation refuses both quaternion dimensions because they now rotate a non-sphere, and they measure 201 px (max 145/255) at 224 px and 28 px at 84 px. ball_y stays excluded there, correctly -- it orients the `ball` prop, which is a sphere in both styles. tests/unit/test_dmcontrol_episode_quat.py asserts every clause of this.

describe.visual_note: The frame is MJWarp's raytrace of the same scene, not dm_control's own raster. Two named mechanisms carry the residual, both measured per surface off MuJoCo's segmentation buffer: (1) the skybox is an 800x4800 gradient with mark="random" specks and MJWarp samples it with one unfiltered tap, which is 48-89% of the frame on cheetah/hopper/walker at mean 4.1-4.7/255 and is what holds SSIM down; (2) the checker floor is MINIFIED and MJWarp has no level-of-detail selection, so where MuJoCo's mipmap shows one grey (far-band luminance spread 0.1 on humanoid) MJWarp paints full contrast (9.7). Suitable for generating training data live -- the frame is a function of the state and the appearance knobs are per-environment tensors. NOT a substitute for a stored dataset when a policy will be evaluated on official dm_control pixels: the train and eval pixel distributions differ by the amount above and nothing here measures what that costs a policy. Closing it needs plane-texture level-of-detail in mujoco_warp's render kernel, which needs ray differentials it does not compute.

DMCFingerTurnEasy.parity_note: parity_interior_min is NOT relaxed: interior-pixel agreement measures exactly 1.000000 -- 0 bad pixels out of 9,834,291 -- over 201 independent draws of 64 states at the shipped default_supersample = 1. What is declared is parity_all_exact_min, and the reason is arithmetic rather than a tolerance -- all-pixel exactness is interior exactness WEIGHTED BY HOW MUCH OF THE FRAME MOVES, and finger-turn_easy's seven movers cover 11.7% of an 84 px frame against cartpole's 2.5%. Measured over those 201 draws: all-pixel 0.9103 at WORST and 0.9119 median, i.e. it CLEARS the shared 0.90 bar on every draw -- the floor is declared so that the margin is the scene's rather than luck's, and it is set from a draw count rather than from one large evaluation, because a rare pixel event reported off a single draw is how MujocoPusher came to declare a floor it then failed 15 times in 101. 100.0% of every disagreeing pixel is inside the ray-cast mover pass and the baked plate is 1.00000 exact on the pixels it owns; the residual is a one-level rim on curved silhouettes, where MuJoCo shades a tessellated capsule per vertex and an analytic per-pixel evaluation lands within a few levels of it. finger-spin (0.9288 worst) and finger-turn_hard (0.9241 worst) are the same renderer with fewer mover pixels and declare nothing. Dropping the supersample IMPROVED all three -- at ss=2 the same draws gave 0.9053 / 0.9249 / 0.9200 -- because an aliased edge is bit-identical to MuJoCo wherever MuJoCo's own MSAA happened to be fully covered, while a blended edge almost never is.

DMCManipulatorBringBall.state_dims_note: Three of fifteen dimensions -- ball_y, target_ball_quat_qw and target_ball_quat_qy -- are EXCLUDED from check_state_dims_matter as render-invariant, under the validated contract that check documents. They are not dead and they are not undrawn: they are geometrically incapable of changing THIS renderer's image, and the reason is a property of the solid rather than of the implementation. All three orient an UNTEXTURED SPHERE -- `ball` is sphere size=.022 on material `self`, `target_ball` is sphere size=.02 on material `target`, and neither material carries a texture -- and a sphere is a surface of revolution about every axis through its centre, so an analytic per-pixel intersector returns the same hit point, the same normal and therefore the same colour for every rotation of it. Exactly, not approximately. NOTHING IS EXCLUDED BY NAME: this class only OFFERS the three (RENDER_INVARIANT_DIMS), and check_state_dims_matter grants the exclusion only after verifying against the compiled model that perturbing the dimension changes nothing but the geom_xmat of SPHERE geoms -- geom_xpos, geom_size, geom_type, every non-sphere orientation and every material, light and camera array bit-identical. A dimension the renderer merely failed to draw moves one of those and is refused. Each granted exclusion is REPORTED in the check's excluded_dims with its reason; none of them is a silent pass. MEASURED, both directions. Under the default (sphere) appearance the three move 0 pixels here at 224 px and at 84 px, while the OFFICIAL renderer moves 896 px at max 55/255 for ball_y and 734 px at max 33/255 for each quaternion slot -- MuJoCo draws a sphere as a TESSELLATED mesh shaded PER VERTEX, so rotating it moves the Gouraud interpolation and the specular vertex. That residual is the same class this family already declares as a one-level rim on curved silhouettes: it is bounded (all-pixel exactness after each perturbation is 0.98275-0.98277 against a 0.98280 baseline, interior-pixel agreement stays 1.000000), and closing it would mean reproducing MuJoCo's icosphere tessellation in the mover pass for EVERY DM Control cell to recover ~800 px at <= 55/255 on one of them. AND THE EXCLUSION EVAPORATES WHEN THE GEOMETRY CHANGES, which is what makes it a statement about spheres rather than about rotation: under target_ball.shape = 0 the target is a BOX, the validation refuses both quaternion dimensions because they now rotate a non-sphere, and they measure 201 px (max 145/255) at 224 px and 28 px at 84 px. ball_y stays excluded there, correctly -- it orients the `ball` prop, which is a sphere in both styles. tests/unit/test_dmcontrol_episode_quat.py asserts every clause of this.
